Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Finance (Stephanie) and Legal (Rishi) to propose a concrete approach. High-level answers below; see specific asks for us internally.

- Invoice split: We can support separate invoices to multiple legal entities. Typical flow is: single Order Form with purchase lines assigned to each entity; Redwood issues separate invoices and tax treatment is applied per invoice. We'll need the exact legal entity names and tax IDs to set this up.
- Net terms: Our default is Net 30. Net 45 is an exception that requires Finance approval for a first-year extension; we can escalate.
- Minimum commit proration: We normally prorate by days remaining in the billing period and then invoice the remainder on the next cycle. We can model a sample calculation for Brightside.

Internal asks (Finance/Legal):
- Stephanie: can you confirm whether we can accept Net 45 on a first-year exception and any revenue recognition implications?

Subject: Internal: suggested commercial language for Brightside (invoice sequencing + net terms)

Team — following up on Laura's note. I sketched a concise set of clauses we can propose to Brightside to minimize back-and-forth:

1) Invoice sequencing: Redwood will issue separate invoices to the legal entities listed on the Order Form. Invoices will reference the same Order Form number and be itemized by product lines. Taxes and VAT (if applicable) will be applied per-invoice based on the billed entity's tax jurisdiction.

2) Net terms: Default Net 30. For first-year customers, Finance may approve Net 45 as a one-time exception. Any Net 45 approval will require a signed payment schedule and an initial prepayment equal to 25% of the first invoice to mitigate credit exposure.

3) Minimum Commit proration: Charges for the first billing period will be prorated by calendar days from the Start Date to the end of the billing cycle. Subsequent invoices will follow the billing cadence in the Order Form.

4) Taxes & Responsibility: Customer is responsible for all sales, use, VAT, and other taxes. Redwood will not gross-up prices unless otherwise agreed in writing. Where Customer provides valid tax exemption documentation, Redwood will apply such exemption at invoice time.

Questions for Legal / Finance:
- Rishi: wording okay for split invoices? Any carve-outs required for withholding taxes or cross-border passthroughs?
- Stephanie: can Finance accept the 25% initial prepay ask for Net 45 approvals? If not, recommend alternate credit mitigation (e.g., SSA/guarantee).

I'll draft the one-page invoice sequencing table for Laura to include in the redline.

Oliver / Brightside procurement — thanks for the draft and patience while we reviewed. Attached is our proposed redline (OrderForm_Redline_20270114.docx). Summary of the material points and requested confirmation: 

- Invoice split & taxes: Redwood confirms we will issue separate invoices to named legal entities on the Order Form. Each invoice will bear taxes appropriate to the billed entity. We added a clause requiring Customer to supply entity legal names and tax IDs prior to the first invoice to avoid misallocation.
- Net terms exception: We can accept Net 45 for the first 12 months as an exception, subject to a prepayment equal to 25% of the amount invoiced in the first cycle. The prepayment will be applied to the first invoice. After 12 months, account reverts to Net 30 unless otherwise approved in writing.
- Minimum commit proration: Language added to prorate by calendar days for initial partial periods; subsequent invoices follow the billing cadence specified in Section 2 of Order Form.

Next steps we propose:
1) Brightside to confirm legal entity names and tax IDs (reply to this thread).
2) Procurement to confirm acceptance of Net 45 + 25% prepay or propose an alternate credit mitigation.
3) If accepted, we will route the redline to DocuSign and Finance will create the billing profile so invoices split correctly.
